Darrell Green

Republican candidate for At-Large Member of the Council of the District of Columbia · Challenger

Retired Metropolitan Police Department officer; small business owner

Darrell Green is a Washington, D.C. native, a retired Metropolitan Police Department officer and a former co-owner of the Adams Mill Bar in Adams Morgan. He was the only candidate for the Republican nomination for the at-large D.C. Council seat in the June 16, 2026 primary. On November 3, 2026, he faces Oye Owolewa (D), Elissa Silverman (I) and Darryl Moch (Statehood Green) for two at-large seats.

Where Green stands

Public safety
Says he supports a people-first approach to policing that focuses on community engagement, trust and accountability, based on his career as a Metropolitan Police officer.
Government accountability
Says his campaign is focused on government integrity, responsive constituent service and accountability at City Hall.

Background

  • Native and lifelong resident of Washington, D.C.
  • Retired officer, Metropolitan Police Department
  • Former co-owner, Adams Mill Bar, Adams Morgan
  • 2026: Republican nominee for D.C. Council At-Large; unopposed in the June 16 primary
